across: Paired by task, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are within noise on single days (v2, v3) and Sol is clearly ahead on 3-day weather fronts (v4: +23.1 pts of hindsight capture, 95% CI [9.0, 48.0]). The untrained Qwen3-4B has the lowest capture throughout.

bench.pitch: Six models in native agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode for the open Beam-⁠1.0 and Qwen3-⁠4B) run a real ERCOT battery's trading desk for three days at a time across 8 real Texas weather fronts, graded in dollars against the hindsight optimum and the battery's real operator.
bench.framework: 0.9.1377 (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna), 0.9.1378 (Qwen3-4B), 0.9.1383 (Gemini 4 Argon) and 0.9.1396 (Beam-1.0)

anchor.label: The anchor, the desk's own optimiser

lead.head: GPT-6.1 Sol captures the most of hindsight:
lead.text: C 27.0% [9.5, 43.8] over its 32 windows, at $4.12 a window. Paired by window, its lead over Gemini 4 Argon: +7.1 pts [+2.8, +11.7].

operator.head: Against the real operator:
operator.text: its own bids, replayed through the same clearing and settlement, capture 7.4%. Ahead of them paired by window, with a CI above zero: GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. Behind, with a CI below zero: Qwen3-4B.

text.halves: Every model scores lower on Jul–Aug than on Jan–May, and that includes Qwen3-4B, whose training predates every window. So the drop reflects harder windows (the Jan–May half includes winter storm Fern), not evidence of training-data contamination. No model the rule covers has a post − pre interval that excludes zero, so all 32 windows lead, by a rule set before any API result.
text.reliability: 304 attempts for 192 model-windows; 112 did not reach the grade (infrastructure ×112). Infrastructure failures were retried; attempts that failed before any model call (a port race in our launcher, $0), Gemini 4 Argon's ended by a transient provider 400 from 18:06 UTC and Beam-1.0's ended by the router's HTTP 402 when its account ran out of credits didn't count toward the two-retry limit (see Deviations). No window is missing.
text.rule: The pre-registered rule that the post-cutoff half leads if the halves differ guards against training-data contamination, so, as read before any API-model result, only a model whose reported training cutoff comes after the first pre-cutoff window (GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and Beam-1.0) can trigger it, when its post − pre interval in C excludes zero.

harness.head: Each model in a native agent harness,
harness.text: through AgentEnv: GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in Codex CLI 0.147.0 with OpenAI's catalog entries for the GPT-6 models; Gemini 4 Argon in Gemini CLI 0.38.2; Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code 2.1.280; Beam-1.0 and Qwen3-4B in OpenCode 1.17.18. The open-weight models: Reflection's Beam-1.0, served by Baseten through the Hugging Face router; Qwen3-4B, served by vLLM 0.29.0 on EC2 GPU boxes (g5.2xlarge, g5.xlarge).

internet.head: No internet.
internet.text: Each run's Docker network is closed to the internet by a host rule, and the model is reached only through a proxy on the host that allows one API and one model per run and refuses provider-side web, code-execution and remote-MCP tools; the agents hold only a placeholder key, which the proxy replaces. Web search and fetch are also off in each harness's own settings; checked from inside the agent containers before the runs.

tools.head: The desk's 11 tools over MCP,
tools.text: beside the harness's own shell, files and planning tools; v4's budget of 100 turns, 14 desk calls a turn and 12 reminders. One run per model per window.

l0.head: The env's control endpoints are not authenticated
l0.text: in this framework release, and an agent's shell can reach the env through its tunnel; no pilot showed an attempt to use them, and the runs are not audited for it.

l1.head: Model plus harness.
l1.text: Each harness's own prompts, tools and context handling are part of what is measured; the harness versions are the ones the framework release pins. Gemini CLI drops a thought signature when it resumes a session, which costs it prompt-cache hits and raises its cost, a known harness issue.

l2.head: The training cutoffs are third-party reports, unconfirmed.
l2.text: The pre-cutoff half reuses v4's 16 windows, which GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and Qwen3-4B also played on the desk's own runner (below).

l3.head: One run per model per window over eight fronts,
l3.text: so the CIs are wide, and a single scarcity front can carry a model's dollars.

l4.head: Cost is list price:
l4.text: tokens at each provider's public price per million, without batch or volume discounts or long-context surcharges; Qwen3-4B's cost is its share of the GPU time.

l5.head: A known env defect, K1, in the benchmark too.
l5.text: An empty reserve-offer list drew a spurious ASO-02 note while the energy curves in the same call were accepted and applied; there is no settlement effect. It is fixed on the head; the frozen runs keep it, and the benchmark plays v4's freeze.

route.head: Route C
route.text: the episodes ran on EC2 boxes with local Docker rather than in Modal sandboxes; the internet was closed by a host rule and a per-run model proxy instead of Modal's network policy (the pre-registration gives the reasons).

errors.head: Provider HTTP 400s
errors.text: 19 of Gemini 4 Argon's 1,488 wake starts (1.28%) drew HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, all on a wake's first request from turn 12 on and more often at larger prompts; the identical request succeeded on replay, so they are transient and infrastructure under the pre-registered rule, and were retried. From 18:06 UTC they did not count toward the two-retry limit, with a safety stop at 6 attempts a window; no window used more than 4.

credits.head: Out of credits
credits.text: the Hugging Face account ran out of prepaid credits at 01:55 UTC on 2026-10-31, after 29 of Beam-1.0's windows had been graded. The router's HTTP 402 then ended four attempts on the 2026-08-26 front, two mid-episode and two before any call; they were reclassified by hand as infrastructure, none counting toward the retry limit, and all four windows were graded once credits were added (the four 2026-08-26 windows all score below zero, S01 included, which ran before the halt).

argon.head: Gemini 4 Argon
argon.text: first deferred for cost, it ran on 2026-10-29 from 16:41 to 19:45 UTC, after the others, by route C on its own box, on agentenv-framework 0.9.1383, whose Gemini harness no longer names its system-prompt file anew each turn (before, every turn start missed the prompt cache).

beam.head: Beam-1.0
beam.text: added after the others for Reflection's Build with Beam contest and run after them, from 23:17 UTC on 2026-10-30 to 02:30 UTC on 2026-10-31, through the Hugging Face router to Baseten at its list price of $0.40 / $1.20 per million input / output tokens, in OpenCode 1.17.18 at effort high on agentenv-framework 0.9.1396, by route C on the Gemini box; its reported training cutoff, 2026-06-30, puts the post-cutoff windows after it.

price.beam: The Hugging Face router publishes no cached-input price for Baseten, so Beam-1.0's list price counts every input token, cached ones included, at the full input price: an upper bound.

cap.splits: C × 100: the share of the hindsight optimum's profit over idle that each model captured, its mean over the windows it finished on each side of the models' reported training cutoffs, Jan–May 2026 (may be in training data) and Jul–Aug 2026 (after every cutoff); 95% CIs, a block bootstrap over the 8 fronts, are in the table below. Grey dashed: the real operator's own bids, replayed through the same clearing and settlement.

table.before: C, hindsight capture, %. Brackets: 95% CIs, a block bootstrap over the 8 weather fronts (four within each side of the cutoffs). Cost a window: the graded attempt's tokens in its harness's own trajectory at the provider's public list price; Qwen3-4B's is GPU time: 4.64 box-hours on EC2 GPU boxes (g5.xlarge at $1.006/h, g5.2xlarge at $1.212/h, EC2 on-demand, us-west-2), each run's share of its box's time while it ran; in all: every attempt, retries and stalls included. Interrupted attempts are costed from the proxy meter, because their last turn never reaches the trajectory. The anchor is the desk's own optimiser re-planning at every wake on the same information; the operator row replays the real operator's bids, disclosed by ERCOT 60 days later, through the same clearing and settlement. Gemini 4 Argon ran on agentenv-framework 0.9.1383. Beam-1.0 ran after the others, through the Hugging Face router, on agentenv-framework 0.9.1396; its account ran out of credits mid-run, and the four attempts the router's HTTP 402 ended were retried as infrastructure.
